- **3rd Annual Pharma Commercial Excellence Summit in Madrid! What an inspiring couple of days exchanging ideas on how AI is reshaping commercial excellence in our industry. I was honored to take the stage with my session "Surfing the AI Wave: How Analytics Professionals Can Lead the Commercial Revolution" — exploring the shift of the Pharma analyst from data executor to strategic orchestrator. I shared two practical, real-world business cases. The first focused on building AI-powered tools from scratch to accelerate new product launches. The second, reimagined the way we forecast pharmaceutical product sales: by embedding AI directly into our Business Analytics workflows, we moved away from fragmented Excel models and heavy external dependencies toward a faster, in-house forecasting engine that turns months of work into days. What struck me most from the discussions is that the future is genuinely exciting — but far from certain. The path ahead stretches from getting the basic fundamentals right all the way to complex, AI-empowered development. We're not there yet, and that's okay. The opportunity is enormous, the uncertainties are real, and the winners will be those willing to experiment, learn fast, and stay humble about how much is still unknown. I'm proud to be part of Bristol Myers Squibb , a company that is genuinely leading the way on this front — and deeply grateful to Jeroen Noordink for the trust and support to develop this cutting-edge work. A heartfelt thank you to Ashish Chandra Saxena for chairing the summit and setting such a thoughtful tone throughout. Equally grateful to Yariv H. for leading a sharp and energizing panel discussion, and to my fellow panelists Arturo Fontangordo Rodríguez and Serkan Ün for the candid, insightful exchange on where AI takes commercial teams next. - **Last two days spent at the Pharma Commercial Excellence Summit in Madrid with Zoe Brown listening to discussions on AI, omnichannel, commercial transformation and customer engagement. What struck me most was that, despite AI appearing in almost every presentation, very few speakers were really talking about technology alone. The recurring themes were much more fundamental: data quality, organisational alignment, adoption, trust and execution. Ashish Chandra Saxena summed it up well when he warned that "if you don't have your foundations in place, AI will simply amplify chaos". It was a reminder that many organisations still have work to do on the fundamentals before they can fully realise the potential of AI. One of the standout sessions for me came from Eduardo Amorim , who demonstrated how he had used Claude Code to build a forecasting solution internally in a fraction of the time and cost traditionally required. The demo itself was impressive, but what stayed with me was what it potentially signals. As AI lowers the barriers to building, testing and iterating; capabilities that once required specialist teams, significant budgets or external support are becoming accessible to far more people. It feels like an important shift, not because expertise becomes less valuable, but because the nature of that expertise is likely to change rapidly. That linked to another theme from the conference. Yariv H. argued that AI should help organisations make decisions faster, not simply generate more analysis. For many organisations, the challenge isn't a lack of information. It's knowing what matters, what to prioritise and what to do next. My biggest takeaway is that the competitive advantage won't come from having access to AI. Everyone will. It will come from combining strong data foundations, genuine customer understanding, human judgement and AI-enabled decision-making in a way that helps organisations learn and adapt faster. And to do that successfully, organisations will need to bring people with them. And as Vikram J. put it: "Adoption is not a product problem. It is a company mindset problem." Thanks to all the speakers for sharing their experiences and perspectives. #Pharma #CommercialExcellence #AI #CustomerInsights #DigitalTransformation #Lumanity ...more ...more**

- **75% try AI in pharma. Only 10% create value. Great to attend the 4th Global Pharma Tech Summit 2026 this week and contribute as both a speaker and moderator alongside leaders across pharma, healthcare, AI and drug discovery. My talk focused on Designing Trust in Health AI: Why Governance Can’t Wait for Regulation. Key themes included: • Governance in healthcare is disciplined decision-making under uncertainty • AI is already delivering value in operational efficiency, clinical decision support and drug discovery • The biggest risks are bias, safety, accountability and the speed of adoption • Regulation is still catching up, so governance must be built into design now, not bolted on later • The shift is from “Is this compliant?” to “Is this safe, fair and explainable at scale?” I also had the pleasure of moderating a panel on AI in drug discovery with Garry Pairaudeau , Nan Fang and Nasir Hannan . Highlights from across the summit included: • Fouad Akkad sharing that while 75% of leaders are experimenting with AI, only 10% are currently creating value and 70% never scale • Trish Parry reflecting on the UK COVID vaccine programme and the challenge of maintaining momentum and shared learning afterwards • Ashish Chandra Saxena emphasising that poor processes and poor data will simply cause AI to amplify problems rather than solve them • Prof. Ashley George encouraging us to learn from countries with much lower HCP-to-citizen ratios and their innovative approaches • Dinesh Sampath Rangaraj from Frost & Sullivan sharing fascinating research into the future impact of AI across pharma and healthcare • Xavier Forceville discussing the challenges of sepsis research and the links with severe COVID cases • Insights from Sarah Jones on leadership in complexity, Liz Ashall-Payne on governance in the regulatory landscape and Babita Evans Kumar MBA on trust and the human side of AI adoption Thank you to the organisers, speakers and attendees for such thoughtful conversations throughout the event. It was insightful to see the evolving AI roadmap and experience agent-based solutions firsthand. AI is now touching every industry and function—and pharma commercial is no exception. Customer-facing teams remains the most impactful channel for influencing prescribing behavior, simultaneously, the most resource-intensive. This makes AI particularly compelling. The potential is clear: 1. Improve productivity 2. Enhance decision-making 3. Drive more personalized engagement However, real-world impact is still being proven at scale. From my perspective, one critical aspect is often underestimated: 👉 Adoption. AI may be “artificial,” but success is deeply human. It changes ways of working and creates uncertainty and trust barriers. And like any transformation, it will face resistance. That said, we all know : 👉 Humans adapt. 👉 Humans learn. 👉 Humans overcome. AI will follow the same path—not just as a technology shift, but as a behavioral and organizational transformation. The real question is not whether AI will create value but how quickly we can unlock it in a scalable, human-centric way. Sebastian F.
